en.statement: For a state with Retry and Catch, AWS Step Functions evaluates Catch before Retry.
en.explanation: Step Functions checks Retry first. It evaluates Catch after retry handling is exhausted or the error has no applicable retrier.

source.title: Handling errors in Step Functions workflows

en.statement: Amazon SQS deletes a message as soon as ReceiveMessage returns it to a consumer.
en.explanation: Receiving an SQS message leaves it in the queue. The consumer sends a separate delete request after processing it.

source.title: Receiving and deleting a message in Amazon SQS

en.statement: An Amazon SQS FIFO queue preserves send order across messages with different MessageGroupId values.
en.explanation: SQS FIFO ordering applies within a message group. Messages in different groups can be processed out of order relative to one another.

source.title: FIFO queue delivery logic in Amazon SQS

en.statement: Amazon API Gateway REST API request validation supports checking header values against a JSON schema.
en.explanation: REST API request validation checks required headers for presence and nonblank values. JSON schema validation applies to the request body.

source.title: Request validation for REST APIs in API Gateway

en.statement: An Amazon API Gateway REST API can select a request mapping template using the request's Content-Type.
en.explanation: For REST API mapping template transformations, API Gateway matches Content-Type to the configured templates and evaluates the matching template for the request payload.

source.title: Mapping template transformations for REST APIs in API Gateway

en.statement: AWS SDK standard retry mode adds jitter to backoff delays to spread retry attempts over time.
en.explanation: Jitter randomizes AWS SDK retry timing, reducing synchronized retry bursts from clients recovering from the same failure.

en.statement: Adaptive retry mode in an AWS SDK rate-limits initial requests too once it detects throttling.
en.explanation: Adaptive mode adds a per-client rate limiter driven by throttling responses, so it can hold back a first attempt, not only a retry. Standard mode never delays the initial request.

en.statement: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams can select a shard by hashing a record's PartitionKey.
en.explanation: For partition-key routing, Kinesis hashes PartitionKey and finds the shard whose hash range contains that hash.

source.title: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams Terminology and concepts

en.statement: Amazon EventBridge PutEvents reports entry-level failures through a failed HTTP response.
en.explanation: PutEvents can return an HTTP success response containing failed entries. The caller checks FailedEntryCount and the error details in Entries.

en.statement: AWS Step Functions resumes a waiting callback task when SendTaskSuccess supplies its matching task token.
en.explanation: The worker sends the task token with its result. Step Functions uses that callback to finish the paused task and continue the execution.

source.title: Discover service integration patterns in Step Functions

en.statement: AWS Lambda assigns a public IPv4 address to a function connected to a public VPC subnet.
en.explanation: A public subnet attachment gives a Lambda function no public IPv4 address. The subnet's route to an internet gateway alone does not provide IPv4 internet access.

source.title: Giving Lambda functions access to resources in an Amazon VPC

en.statement: A Lambda on-success destination receives the function's result inside an invocation record.
en.explanation: Lambda puts the returned value in responsePayload, alongside information about the asynchronous invocation.

source.title: Capturing records of Lambda asynchronous invocations

en.statement: A Lambda SQS handler can list failed message IDs in batchItemFailures for a partial batch response.
en.explanation: Enable ReportBatchItemFailures on the event source mapping and return failed IDs as itemIdentifier entries. Lambda then retries the failed messages.

source.title: Handling errors for an SQS event source in Lambda

en.statement: AWS Lambda Invoke returns an HTTP error status when a synchronous handler throws an exception.
en.explanation: A synchronous Invoke handler failure appears in FunctionError and the response payload. The HTTP status reflects the invocation request's success.

en.statement: Lambda reserved concurrency prepares execution environments before incoming invocations.
en.explanation: Reserved concurrency sets aside and caps concurrent execution capacity. Provisioned concurrency pre-initializes environments to reduce cold starts.

source.title: Configuring reserved concurrency for a function

en.statement: AWS Lambda retains /tmp files when it reuses the same execution environment for another invocation.
en.explanation: The /tmp directory survives an execution environment's freeze and reuse. Code can reuse cached files while that environment remains available.

source.title: Understanding the Lambda execution environment lifecycle

en.statement: Lambda functions packaged as container images can load dependencies from attached Lambda layers.
en.explanation: Lambda layers attach to functions packaged as .zip archives. A container image includes its dependencies during the image build.

en.statement: Increasing a Lambda function's configured memory also increases its allocated CPU resources.
en.explanation: Lambda allocates CPU power in proportion to configured memory, so memory tuning also changes the compute available to the code.

en.statement: Lambda runs an event source mapping's FilterCriteria evaluation inside the function handler.
en.explanation: The Lambda service evaluates event source mapping filters before invoking the function. The handler receives records that pass those filters.

source.title: Control which events Lambda sends to your function

en.statement: A DynamoDB Query uses equality on the partition key in its KeyConditionExpression.
en.explanation: DynamoDB Query targets a specified partition key value. Its key condition supplies that value through an equality comparison.

source.title: Key condition expressions for the Query operation in DynamoDB

en.statement: A DynamoDB Query FilterExpression reduces the read capacity consumed by the request.
en.explanation: DynamoDB applies FilterExpression after reading the items, so filtering changes the returned results rather than the read capacity consumed.

source.title: Filter expressions for the Query operation in DynamoDB

en.statement: DynamoDB supports strongly consistent Query requests against global secondary indexes.
en.explanation: DynamoDB global secondary indexes provide eventually consistent reads. A Query requesting strong consistency on a GSI is rejected.

en.statement: DynamoDB PutItem can use attribute_not_exists to protect an existing item from replacement.
en.explanation: A PutItem condition using attribute_not_exists on the partition key fails when an item with that primary key already exists.

en.statement: DynamoDB removes expired items from read results as soon as their TTL timestamp passes.
en.explanation: DynamoDB deletes TTL-expired items asynchronously. Reads can return expired items while they await deletion.

source.title: Using time to live (TTL) in DynamoDB

en.statement: The DynamoDB low-level API sends an N attribute's numeric value as a string.
en.explanation: The N tag identifies a number even though its wire value is a string. DynamoDB still treats the stored attribute numerically.

en.statement: An Amazon S3 GetObject call for the current version reflects a successfully completed object overwrite.
en.explanation: Amazon S3 makes successful object overwrites visible to subsequent reads through strong read-after-write consistency.

en.statement: Amazon S3 DeleteObject with a key alone permanently removes existing versions in a versioning-enabled bucket.
en.explanation: In a versioning-enabled bucket, DeleteObject with a key alone creates a delete marker. Existing object versions remain stored.

en.statement: Amazon RDS Data API commits an ExecuteStatement change when the caller omits transactionId.
en.explanation: An ExecuteStatement call with transactionId absent runs outside an explicit Data API transaction. RDS Data API commits changes from that call.

en.statement: Amazon OpenSearch Service analyzes a term query's input using the target field's text analyzer.
en.explanation: An OpenSearch term query compares its input as an exact term rather than analyzing it as full text. Input should match the indexed term.

en.statement: An Amazon Cognito user pool issues AWS access keys after a user signs in.
en.explanation: After a successful sign-in, a Cognito user pool returns an ID token, an access token and a refresh token. Apps can exchange those tokens for temporary AWS credentials in a separate step.

source.title: Understanding user pool JSON web tokens (JWTs)

en.statement: An Amazon Cognito access token uses a different signing key than the ID token from the same session.
en.explanation: Cognito signs access and ID tokens with separate keys. Code selects the verification key from the token's kid value.

en.statement: Setting apiKeyRequired on an Amazon API Gateway REST API method enables IAM authorization for that method.
en.explanation: apiKeyRequired enables REST API key enforcement. The method's authorizationType setting selects its authorization mechanism.

en.statement: An explicit Deny in an applicable IAM policy overrides an Allow for the same request.
en.explanation: AWS rejects a request covered by an applicable explicit Deny even when another applicable policy grants that access.

en.statement: An IAM permissions boundary can grant actions through its own Allow statements.
en.explanation: A permissions boundary limits permissions available to an IAM entity. Its Allow statements set a ceiling rather than grant access.

en.statement: AWS STS AssumeRole returns temporary credentials that include a session token.
en.explanation: AssumeRole returns an access key ID, secret access key and session token. Code supplies that token when using the temporary credentials.

en.statement: AWS STS GetCallerIdentity returns the same ARN for assumed-role credentials as for the IAM user who assumed the role.
en.explanation: With assumed-role credentials, GetCallerIdentity returns the assumed-role session's ARN. It identifies the active session rather than the IAM user who assumed the role.

en.statement: AWS Signature Version 4 sends the caller's secret access key with the signed API request.
en.explanation: SigV4 derives a signing key from the secret access key and sends a calculated signature. The secret access key stays with the signer.

source.title: Create a signed AWS API request

en.statement: A caller passing an execution role to AWS Lambda CreateFunction needs iam:PassRole permission.
en.explanation: iam:PassRole permits the caller to hand that execution role to Lambda. It authorizes passing the role to the service during function creation.

source.title: Grant a user permissions to pass a role to an AWS service

en.statement: A Lambda function's resource-based policy grants its handler permission to call DynamoDB PutItem.
en.explanation: A Lambda function receives DynamoDB permissions through its execution role. Its resource-based policy grants other principals access to the function.

en.statement: A DynamoDB IAM policy can use dynamodb:LeadingKeys to restrict access by partition key value.
en.explanation: For supported item operations, dynamodb:LeadingKeys limits requests to permitted partition key values, so a caller can be restricted to its own items.

source.title: Using IAM policy conditions for fine-grained access control

en.statement: AWS KMS GenerateDataKey supports returning a plaintext data key along with its KMS-encrypted copy.
en.explanation: Use the plaintext data key to encrypt application data, then discard it. Keep the encrypted copy so the data key can be recovered later.

en.statement: AWS KMS treats encryption context keys and values as case-insensitive during decryption.
en.explanation: Decrypting symmetric KMS ciphertext uses the encryption context supplied during encryption, with exact case-sensitive matches for its keys and values.

en.statement: AWS KMS propagates a new grant's permissions with strong consistency after CreateGrant succeeds.
en.explanation: New KMS grants propagate with eventual consistency. A caller can pass the returned grant token to use the grant before propagation finishes.

en.statement: Amazon S3 initializes a new bucket's object encryption configuration with SSE-S3 by default.
en.explanation: New S3 buckets start with SSE-S3 default encryption, so uploads receive server-side encryption. Developers can configure a different supported default.

source.title: Using server-side encryption with Amazon S3 managed keys (SSE-S3)

en.statement: Amazon S3 stores the customer-provided encryption key with an object uploaded using SSE-C.
en.explanation: For SSE-C, S3 discards the supplied key after using it. The caller retains the key and provides it again for operations that decrypt the object.

source.title: Using server-side encryption with customer-provided keys (SSE-C)

en.statement: Amazon S3 GetObject on an SSE-KMS object needs the caller to hold kms:Decrypt on its KMS key.
en.explanation: A caller needs kms:Decrypt on the object's KMS key as well as s3:GetObject, because that key protects the data key S3 stored with the object. Without it, the download is denied.

source.title: Using server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS)

en.statement: With policy-based access, AWS KMS checks the key policy and the caller's IAM policy for cross-account use.
en.explanation: The key-owning account authorizes the external principal in its key policy. The caller's account delegates that permission through an IAM policy.

source.title: Allowing users in other accounts to use a KMS key

en.statement: Rotating an AWS KMS key rewrites existing ciphertext with the key's newly generated key material.
en.explanation: KMS rotation changes material used for new encryption rather than rewriting existing ciphertext. Decryption uses the material that originally encrypted the data.

en.statement: AWS KMS supports automatic rotation for asymmetric KMS keys used for encryption.
en.explanation: Automatic KMS rotation applies to eligible symmetric encryption keys. Rotate an asymmetric key by creating a replacement key and updating application references.

en.statement: AWS Private CA IssueCertificate returns the issued certificate's PEM data in its response.
en.explanation: IssueCertificate returns a certificate ARN. Retrieve the issued certificate with GetCertificate after issuance completes.

en.statement: Amazon EC2 CreateKeyPair returns the private key material in its successful response.
en.explanation: Save the private key returned by CreateKeyPair. EC2 retains the matching public key for instances that use the key pair.

en.statement: CloudWatch Logs applies a new data protection policy to previously ingested sensitive log events.
en.explanation: A data protection policy applies to log events ingested after the policy takes effect. Older events retain their original masking status.

source.title: Help protect sensitive log data with masking

en.statement: CloudWatch Logs GetLogEvents reveals masked values by default for a caller with logs:Unmask permission.
en.explanation: A caller with logs:Unmask permission sets unmask=true on GetLogEvents to request the original sensitive values. Permission alone leaves the default masking in place.

en.statement: Lambda function code calls KMS Decrypt to read environment values protected with client-side encryption.
en.explanation: Client-side encrypted Lambda environment values reach the handler as ciphertext. Function code calls KMS Decrypt to recover the plaintext.

en.statement: AWS Secrets Manager rotation refreshes cached values in the AWS parameters and secrets Lambda extension.
en.explanation: The extension keeps a cached secret until its configured TTL expires. Rotating a secret does not push a new value into that cache.

source.title: Use Secrets Manager secrets in Lambda functions

en.statement: AWS Secrets Manager logs the returned SecretString in CloudTrail's GetSecretValue event.
en.explanation: Secrets Manager excludes SecretString and SecretBinary values from CloudTrail records. The audit event tracks the API call rather than returning the secret's contents.

en.statement: AWS Systems Manager keeps an advanced parameter's Expiration timestamp when the parameter value changes.
en.explanation: A value update preserves the Expiration policy's timestamp. Change or remove the policy to adjust when Systems Manager deletes the parameter.

source.title: Assigning parameter policies in Parameter Store

en.statement: AWS CodeBuild resolves env/secrets-manager references into environment values for build commands.
en.explanation: A buildspec can name a Secrets Manager secret under env/secrets-manager. CodeBuild retrieves its value under the chosen environment variable name.

en.statement: AWS CodeBuild supports masking a secret after build code base64-encodes the retrieved env/secrets-manager value.
en.explanation: CodeBuild masks the exact secret value it retrieves. A transformed value, such as a base64-encoded copy, can appear in logs, so build code handles sanitization.

en.statement: DynamoDB can return a permitted subset for a request that asks for attributes denied by dynamodb:Attributes.
en.explanation: dynamodb:Attributes restricts the attributes a caller requests. A request outside that permission is denied; IAM does not redact it into an allowed subset.

source.title: Using IAM policy conditions for fine-grained access control

en.statement: Amazon S3 supports tenant-specific object prefixes in IAM policies that use ${aws:PrincipalTag/tenant}.
en.explanation: IAM substitutes the caller's tenant tag into the S3 object resource ARN. An allowed ARN ending in that tenant's prefix restricts the covered object operations.

source.title: IAM policy elements: Variables and tags

en.statement: A Python Lambda .zip package for handler app.handler places app.py at the archive root.
en.explanation: For a handler configured as app.handler, Lambda imports app.py as a top-level module. Put that file at the root of the deployment archive.

source.title: Working with .zip file archives for Python Lambda functions

en.statement: AWS Lambda extracts a layer's archive into /opt in the function's execution environment.
en.explanation: Layer contents land under /opt. Package dependencies in the directory layout expected by the function's runtime so it can find them.

en.statement: Lambda supplies a runtime interface client to functions built from a Debian base image.
en.explanation: For a Lambda image built from a Debian base image, include a runtime interface client during the image build. That client communicates with the Lambda Runtime API.

source.title: Create a Lambda function using a container image

en.statement: Lambda gives container functions a writable root filesystem for generated application files.
en.explanation: Lambda runs container images with a read-only root filesystem. Code writes temporary files to /tmp instead.

source.title: Create a Lambda function using a container image

en.statement: An AWS CodeArtifact authorization token can access repositories across its issuing domain.
en.explanation: CodeArtifact tokens are scoped to a domain, so a token can authenticate to its repositories subject to the caller's repository permissions.

en.statement: AWS CodeBuild selects build runtimes from runtime-versions in the build phase of a buildspec.
en.explanation: CodeBuild reads runtime-versions from the buildspec's install phase. It selects runtimes available in the chosen build image.

en.statement: AWS CodeBuild includes the paths under cache/paths in the build's output artifact.
en.explanation: cache/paths identifies files to cache for future builds. The buildspec's artifacts section selects the build output files.

en.statement: Elastic Beanstalk reads .ebextensions configuration files written in YAML or JSON.
en.explanation: Put files with a .config extension under .ebextensions in the application bundle. Elastic Beanstalk parses them to configure the environment.

source.title: Advanced environment customization with configuration files (.ebextensions)

en.statement: AWS AppConfig supports a JSON Schema validator for checking free form configuration before deployment.
en.explanation: AppConfig checks free form configuration against the schema you supply. A schema validation failure blocks deploying that configuration.

en.statement: A Lambda validator's normal return of an error message signals validation failure to AWS AppConfig.
en.explanation: A Lambda validator signals AppConfig validation failure by throwing an exception. A successful return containing an error message does not signal that failure.

en.statement: AWS SAM CLI sam local start-api runs a function's Lambda authorizer locally before the function.
en.explanation: A request to the local endpoint goes to the authorizer first, and the SAM CLI invokes the function only when authorization succeeds. Local authorizer behavior can differ from the deployed one.

source.title: Introduction to testing with sam local start-api

en.statement: AWS SAM sam local invoke redirects the function's AWS SDK calls to built-in service emulators.
en.explanation: SAM runs the Lambda function locally. Its SDK calls target their configured endpoints, so tests can reach live AWS resources unless you supply mocks or emulators.

source.title: How to test serverless functions and applications

en.statement: Amazon API Gateway REST API TestInvokeMethod needs a deployed stage to test a configured method.
en.explanation: TestInvokeMethod simulates a configured REST API method before API deployment. It lets the developer test the method through the API Gateway management interface.

source.title: Invoke REST APIs in API Gateway

en.statement: A REST API mock integration in Amazon API Gateway returns data produced by its response mapping template.
en.explanation: For a REST API mock integration, an integration response mapping template generates a response body for the caller, allowing a developer to simulate backend output.

source.title: Mock integrations for REST APIs in API Gateway

en.statement: Amazon API Gateway REST API stages use the latest saved integration settings for incoming requests.
en.explanation: A stage serves its associated deployment. REST API integration changes take effect there after a new deployment is associated with the stage.

source.title: Create a deployment for a REST API in API Gateway

en.statement: AWS Step Functions TestState supports inspectionData.request at DEBUG level for an HTTP Task.
en.explanation: TestState uses TRACE for HTTP request details in inspectionData.request. DEBUG shows intermediate state input and output processing results.

en.statement: AWS Lambda Invoke with InvocationType=DryRun checks the caller's lambda:InvokeFunction permission.
en.explanation: DryRun validates the request parameters and the caller's permission to invoke the function. It provides a permission check while leaving the handler unexecuted.

en.statement: AWS SAM CLI sam remote test-event stores shareable Lambda test events in the EventBridge schema registry.
en.explanation: Users of the same AWS account can get, list, put or delete these shareable events and pass one to sam remote invoke to test the deployed function in the cloud.

source.title: Introduction to cloud testing with sam remote test-event

en.statement: AWS CodeBuild builds test reports from test runner output printed to the build's standard output.
en.explanation: CodeBuild reads test result files selected by reports/files in the buildspec. Configure the test runner to write a supported report format.

en.statement: AWS AppSync EvaluateMappingTemplate sends the evaluated request to the resolver's configured data source.
en.explanation: EvaluateMappingTemplate renders a template against a mock context you supply and returns evaluationResult. It runs no request against the resolver's data source.

source.title: Testing and debugging resolvers in AWS AppSync (VTL)

en.statement: AWS Lambda freezes a published version's environment variables at the values present during publication.
en.explanation: PublishVersion captures environment settings with the function version. Change $LATEST and publish a new version to use different values.

en.statement: Lambda resolves an image tag to a specific image digest when a developer deploys container function code.
en.explanation: Moving the ECR tag afterward leaves the configured function on that digest. Call UpdateFunctionCode to deploy the tag's updated image.

en.statement: Amazon API Gateway can associate several REST API stages with the same deployment.
en.explanation: Several stages can refer to a shared REST API deployment, letting a developer expose the same deployed API through different stage names.

en.statement: AWS CloudFormation waits for ExecuteChangeSet before applying an update described in a change set.
en.explanation: Creating an update change set prepares a preview of the proposed changes. ExecuteChangeSet tells CloudFormation to apply that update.

source.title: Update CloudFormation stacks using change sets

en.statement: AWS CloudFormation drift detection compares omitted resource properties with their service defaults.
en.explanation: Drift detection checks explicitly configured property values. Set a property in the template, even to its default, to include it in drift tracking.

source.title: Detect unmanaged configuration changes to stacks and resources with drift detection

en.statement: AWS CloudFormation creates a resource that uses Ref to point to a resource whose condition evaluates to false.
en.explanation: CloudFormation creates a conditional resource only when its condition is true. A resource that depends on an uncreated resource can't be created either, whatever its own condition says.

en.statement: AWS SAM creates an execution role for AWS::Serverless::Function when the template omits its Role property.
en.explanation: SAM generates an IAM role for that function when Role is omitted. The generated role's logical ID combines the function's logical ID with Role.

en.statement: AWS CodeDeploy sends an application test payload as the event for an AWS SAM PreTraffic hook.
en.explanation: The hook event supplies DeploymentId and LifecycleEventHookExecutionId. The hook code builds its own application payload when invoking the version under test.

source.title: Create a file for your BeforeAllowTraffic Lambda function

en.statement: Amazon API Gateway REST API mapping templates read stage variables through $context.stageVariables.
en.explanation: A REST API mapping template reads a stage variable as $stageVariables.name or $stageVariables['name']. The stage supplies the corresponding value.

source.title: Variables for data transformations for API Gateway

en.statement: AWS Lambda requires versions behind a weighted alias to share the same execution role.
en.explanation: A weighted alias routes invocations between published versions with matching execution roles. Align those roles before adding the additional version.

source.title: Implement Lambda canary deployments using a weighted alias

en.statement: AWS CloudFormation ValidateTemplate verifies that an EC2 instance's KeyName names an existing key pair.
en.explanation: ValidateTemplate checks that the template is valid JSON or YAML. Whether a named EC2 key pair exists comes to light when CloudFormation creates or updates the stack.

en.statement: AWS CodePipeline's service role needs codestar-connections:UseConnection besides codeconnections:UseConnection.
en.explanation: The CodePipeline docs require both actions on the connection ARN: some operations call codestar-connections:UseConnection and others call codeconnections:UseConnection.

source.title: CodeStarSourceConnection for Bitbucket Cloud, GitHub, GitHub Enterprise Server, GitLab.com, and GitLab self-managed actions

en.statement: AWS CodeBuild includes the artifacts/base-directory folder around its matched output files.
en.explanation: CodeBuild packages matching files and subdirectories from artifacts/base-directory. It omits the matched base directory itself from the artifact.

en.statement: AWS CodePipeline runs actions with the same runOrder in parallel within a stage.
en.explanation: Assign matching runOrder values to actions that run together. CodePipeline waits for that action group before starting a higher runOrder group.

en.statement: In SUPERSEDED mode, AWS CodePipeline can replace an execution while its action is still running.
en.explanation: CodePipeline supersedes waiting executions between stages. An execution running actions inside a stage keeps that stage until its work finishes.

en.statement: AWS CodeDeploy can use a Lambda alias name as TargetVersion in a deployment's AppSpec file.
en.explanation: A Lambda AppSpec's target version is a published function version, identified by its version number. The deployment's Alias property names the alias separately.

en.statement: AWS CodeDeploy shifts Lambda deployment traffic by changing the version weights behind a function alias.
en.explanation: A Lambda deployment uses the alias's routing weights to move traffic toward the new version at the rate selected in the deployment configuration.

source.title: Step 3: Deploy the updated Lambda function

en.statement: AWS CodeDeploy assigns a new deployment ID when rolling back to a previous application revision.
en.explanation: Rollback redeploys a previously deployed revision as a new deployment. Its separate deployment ID lets you track that recovery operation.

source.title: Redeploy and roll back a deployment with CodeDeploy

en.statement: AWS Elastic Beanstalk launches a temporary Auto Scaling group for an immutable application deployment.
en.explanation: Elastic Beanstalk places the new instances in a separate group while the original instances remain available. It evaluates the new fleet before completing the deployment.

en.statement: Amazon API Gateway applies a REST API canary's stageVariableOverrides to production-release requests.
en.explanation: Canary overrides change the stage variable values used for canary requests. Production-release requests keep the stage's production values.

en.statement: Amazon API Gateway REST API stage variables can select Lambda functions in another AWS account.
en.explanation: A Lambda function selected through a REST API stage variable belongs to the API's AWS account. This stage-variable feature excludes cross-account Lambda targets.

source.title: API Gateway stage variables reference for REST APIs in API Gateway

en.statement: AWS Lambda counts throttled invocation requests in the function's Errors metric.
en.explanation: Lambda records throttled requests in Throttles. Errors counts invocations that run and end with a function error, such as an exception or timeout.

source.title: Types of metrics for Lambda functions

en.statement: AWS Lambda reports IteratorAge using the last record in a Kinesis event sent to the function.
en.explanation: IteratorAge measures elapsed time from the stream receiving that record to the event source mapping sending its batch to Lambda.

source.title: Types of metrics for Lambda functions

en.statement: AWS Lambda returns base64-encoded execution log text in Invoke's LogResult when LogType=Tail.
en.explanation: Request LogType=Tail for a synchronous invocation, then base64-decode LogResult to inspect the returned execution log excerpt.

en.statement: CloudWatch Logs Insights discovers fields in JSON log events in Standard log groups by default.
en.explanation: JSON field discovery exposes structured values for queries. Developers can filter on a discovered field instead of parsing its raw log text.

en.statement: CloudWatch embedded metric format requires log publishers to have cloudwatch:PutMetricData permission.
en.explanation: An embedded metric format publisher sends logs with logs:PutLogEvents. CloudWatch extracts the metrics; the publisher needs no separate PutMetricData permission.

en.statement: A CloudWatch metric alarm using TreatMissingData=ignore retains its state during an empty evaluation.
en.explanation: If the evaluation range contains no data points, the ignore setting preserves the prior alarm state instead of declaring INSUFFICIENT_DATA.

source.title: Configuring how CloudWatch alarms treat missing data

en.statement: AWS CloudTrail event history shows the data events collected by a configured trail.
en.explanation: CloudTrail event history shows management events. A trail's data-event configuration does not add those data events to event history.

en.statement: AWS CloudFormation DescribeStackEvents lists the stack's oldest events first in its response.
en.explanation: DescribeStackEvents returns events in reverse chronological order. Read their timestamps to reconstruct the sequence leading to a deployment failure.

en.statement: Amazon API Gateway REST API IntegrationLatency measures the gateway's complete request processing time.
en.explanation: IntegrationLatency measures the backend request-response interval. API Gateway's Latency metric includes that interval plus the gateway's other processing overhead.

source.title: Amazon API Gateway dimensions and metrics

en.statement: AWS X-Ray can search trace metadata values through filter expressions passed to GetTraceSummaries.
en.explanation: X-Ray indexes annotations for trace filtering. Metadata remains stored with the trace but is excluded from the search index.

en.statement: AWS X-Ray sampling rules can match requests at a trace's entry point by HTTP method and URL path.
en.explanation: HTTP method and URL path are request-match criteria in an X-Ray sampling rule. They let the developer apply a sampling policy to particular routes.

en.statement: Lambda active tracing records function code's outbound HTTP requests as subsegments by default.
en.explanation: Active tracing records Lambda invocation timing. Application instrumentation supplies detailed subsegments for calls made by the function code.

source.title: Visualize Lambda function invocations using AWS X-Ray

en.statement: CloudWatch treats one metric name published with two different dimension values as two distinct metrics.
en.explanation: Namespace, metric name and dimensions together identify a CloudWatch metric, and statistics come back only for the dimension combinations that were published.

en.statement: CloudWatch schedules recurring SNS notifications for an alarm that remains in the ALARM state.
en.explanation: CloudWatch invokes the SNS action when the alarm changes into its configured state. Remaining in ALARM does not schedule repeated SNS notifications.

en.statement: A CloudWatch composite alarm can combine ALARM and OK tests in the same AlarmRule expression.
en.explanation: AlarmRule evaluates state tests for referenced alarms using Boolean operators. Mixing ALARM and OK tests lets a developer express conditional alert criteria.

en.statement: CloudWatch Logs supports a default metric-filter value for a metric that has configured dimensions.
en.explanation: CloudWatch Logs excludes default values for metric filters that publish dimensions. Default values are available for filters that omit dimensions.

source.title: Filter pattern syntax for metric filters

en.statement: Amazon ECS automatically uses task definition healthCheck settings in place of an image's Dockerfile HEALTHCHECK.
en.explanation: Health-check parameters in the ECS container definition override the check embedded in its image. The ECS agent evaluates the configured task-definition check.

source.title: Determine Amazon ECS task health using container health checks

en.statement: An Application Load Balancer sends HEAD health-check requests to a target group with ProtocolVersion=HTTP1.
en.explanation: For HTTP1 target groups, Application Load Balancer health checks send GET requests to the configured path. Implement the health endpoint for that method.

source.title: Health checks for Application Load Balancer target groups

en.statement: Amazon ECS counts later health-check failures after a successful check during startPeriod.
en.explanation: A successful check during startPeriod marks the container healthy. Subsequent failures count toward retries even if the configured start period is still running.

source.title: Determine Amazon ECS task health using container health checks

en.statement: Amazon SNS uses OR across property names in a subscription filter policy that omits the $or operator.
en.explanation: SNS combines conditions on different filter-policy properties with AND unless an explicit $or relationship applies. A matching message satisfies the property conditions together.

en.statement: With gzip caching enabled, Amazon CloudFront reduces Accept-Encoding: gzip,deflate to gzip in cache keys by default.
en.explanation: CloudFront includes the normalized compression header in the cache key. For a gzip-enabled cache policy, extra encodings such as deflate do not create separate cache entries.

en.statement: A browser can keep serving a cached file after Amazon CloudFront finishes invalidating that file.
en.explanation: CloudFront invalidation removes the file from its edge caches. A copy in a browser's cache can remain usable until that cache entry expires.

en.statement: Amazon API Gateway enables POST caching by default when a developer turns on REST API stage-level caching.
en.explanation: The REST API stage's default method cache setting applies to GET methods. Enable a method override explicitly to cache POST responses.

source.title: Cache settings for REST APIs in API Gateway

en.statement: Amazon DynamoDB UpdateItem applies numeric ADD updates atomically under concurrent writes.
en.explanation: Use an ADD update expression to increment the stored counter value inside DynamoDB. Concurrent increments avoid a client-side read-modify-write race.

source.title: Use atomic counter operations in DynamoDB with an AWS SDK

en.statement: Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) supports cache hits for GetItem requests with ConsistentRead=true.
en.explanation: DAX forwards a GetItem request with ConsistentRead=true to DynamoDB. It returns the response to the client but does not cache that result.

en.statement: Amazon SQS long polling queries the same weighted subset of servers that short polling queries.
en.explanation: With long polling, ReceiveMessage queries the full set of SQS servers for the queue. Broader server coverage reduces false empty responses.

source.title: Amazon SQS short and long polling

en.statement: Amazon ECS supports CPU use above a container's cpu reservation for Linux containers hosted on Amazon EC2.
en.explanation: For Linux containers on EC2, the container-level cpu setting supplies relative CPU shares. Spare host CPU can be used above that reservation, subject to task-level limits.

en.statement: For MySQL, Amazon RDS Proxy pins the session when a client executes CREATE TEMPORARY TABLE.
en.explanation: The temporary table's state belongs to that database session. RDS Proxy preserves it by keeping subsequent transactions on the same underlying connection.

en.statement: In a reused Python Lambda environment, the REPORT line's Max Memory Used measures the current invocation's peak.
en.explanation: For invocations sharing a Python Lambda execution environment, Max Memory Used reports the highest memory use across those invocations. An earlier peak can affect a later REPORT line.

source.title: Log and monitor Python Lambda functions
